etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English curteis, from Old French curteis (French courtois), from cort (“court”).

definitions.definition: Showing regard or thought for others; especially, displaying good manners or etiquette.

quote.citation: 1818, John Keats, “Book III”, in Endymion: A Poetic Romance, London:  […]  T[homas] Miller, […] for Taylor and Hessey, […], →OCLC, page 149, lines 932–935:
quote.text: Nectar ran / In courteous fountains to all cups outreach'd; / And plunder'd vines, teeming exhaustless, pleach'd / New growth about each shell and pendent lyre; [...]
